Decode Tumour Fraction, Ploidy and Copy-Number Segments from Corrected Bins

Source: R/depth.R
rduckhts_depth_state_solutions.Rd

Fits the copy-number state model of ichorCNA (Adalsteinsson, Ha, Freeman et al. 2017; GavinHaLab/ichorCNA tag v0.6.1) to each sample's kept corrected bins: a hidden Markov model over copy numbers 1 to `max_cn` with a Student's t emission on the log ratio, whose state means follow from the normal fraction `n` and tumour ploidy `phi`, fitted by expectation maximisation with the upstream priors from every start of `ploidies` x `normal_fractions`. Each start gives one solution, ranked by its objective (data log-likelihood plus log prior). [rduckhts_depth_state_solutions()] returns the solutions; [rduckhts_depth_state_segments()] returns their Viterbi segments.

Usage

rduckhts_depth_state_solutions(
  con,
  bins_table,
  normal_fractions = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9),
  ploidies = c(2, 3),
  max_cn = 7,
  txn_e = 0.9999999,
  txn_strength = 1e+07,
  max_iter = 20,
  min_segment_bins = 50,
  alt_fraction_threshold = 0.05,
  close_margin = 10,
  max_bins = 1e+06,
  table_name = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

rduckhts_depth_state_segments(
  con,
  bins_table,
  normal_fractions = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9),
  ploidies = c(2, 3),
  max_cn = 7,
  txn_e = 0.9999999,
  txn_strength = 1e+07,
  max_iter = 20,
  min_segment_bins = 50,
  alt_fraction_threshold = 0.05,
  close_margin = 10,
  max_bins = 1e+06,
  table_name = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

con

A DuckDB connection with DuckHTS loaded.

bins_table

Name of a table or view of corrected bins with `sample_id`, `chrom`, `start`, `end`, `log2_ratio` and `kept`, such as the output of [rduckhts_depth_bins()]. Restrict contigs and remove problem bins in SQL first.

normal_fractions

Starts of the normal fraction, each in (0, 1).

ploidies

Starts of the tumour ploidy, each in \[1, 10\]; the EM starts from their floor. A normal start of 0.95 runs only at ploidy 2, as upstream.

max_cn

Highest copy-number state, a whole number in \[2, 20\].

txn_e

Self-transition probability in (0, 1).

txn_strength

Transition pseudo-counts, positive.

max_iter

EM iteration cap, a whole number in \[2, 1000\].

min_segment_bins, alt_fraction_threshold

The guard's two thresholds.

close_margin

Objective difference below which a lower-ranked solution is `close_to_best`.

max_bins

Kept bins one sample may hold; the model holds about `max_cn * 28 + 40` bytes a bin.

table_name

Optional table to create instead of returning a data frame.

overwrite

Whether `table_name` may replace an existing table.

Value

A data frame (or invisible `TRUE` when `table_name` is given). Solutions have one row per sample and start: `sample_id`, `solution` (rank, 1 is best), `start_normal`, `start_ploidy`, `normal_fraction`, `tumour_fraction`, `ploidy`, `log_likelihood`, `altered_fraction`, `iterations`, `status`, `segments`, `bins`, `upstream` and `method`. Segments have one row per sample, solution and segment: the solution columns through `status`, then `chrom`, `start`, `end`, `bins`, `state` (the copy number of the Viterbi state), `copy_number` (after upstream's integer correction of high-level amplifications), `median_log2_ratio`, `upstream` and `method`.

Details

The model learns from autosomal bins (contigs whose `duckhts_contig_key()` is not X, Y or MT) and decodes every kept bin. A kept bin without a ratio takes every state with likelihood 1, as upstream carries it. Upstream's guard sets the fraction to zero (`status` `guard_zero`) when the longest altered training segment has at most `min_segment_bins` bins and at most `alt_fraction_threshold` of the training bins are altered; a solution ranked below the best with an objective within `close_margin` of it is `close_to_best`, the rest are `ok`. A sample without copy-number change therefore reports no fraction, by the guard or by a fit whose normal fraction is near 1; in that fit the state means lie within the noise of each other and whole chromosomes can take any state, so its copy numbers are not evidence. Fraction and ploidy trade against each other, so all solutions are returned; a ploidy-3 explanation of a ploidy-2 genome usually ranks second. The port and its kept upstream quirks are documented in the DuckHTS catalog entry and `design/depth_fraction_lane.md`.

Examples

con <- rduckhts_connect()
DBI::dbExecute(con, paste(
  "CREATE TEMP TABLE bins AS SELECT 'S1' AS sample_id, CAST(c AS VARCHAR) AS chrom,",
  "b * 1000000 AS start, (b + 1) * 1000000 AS \"end\", true AS kept,",
  "log2(CASE WHEN c = 8 THEN 1.15 ELSE 1 END) +",
  "0.05 * (((b * 37 + c * 11) % 100) / 50.0 - 1) AS log2_ratio",
  "FROM range(1, 23) t(c), range(0, 60) r(b)"
))
#> [1] 1320
best <- rduckhts_depth_state_solutions(con, "bins")
best[best$solution == 1, c("tumour_fraction", "ploidy", "status")]
#>   tumour_fraction   ploidy status
#> 5       0.1011181 2.009539     ok
segments <- rduckhts_depth_state_segments(con, "bins")
segments[segments$solution == 1 & segments$chrom == "8", c("chrom", "copy_number", "bins")]
#>    chrom copy_number bins
#> 21     8           5   60
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
